claims.claim: Revenues totaled $31.6 billion, up 2.3% from the year-ago quarter.
Diluted EPS from continuing operations was $0.66, compared to $0.62 in the year-ago quarter.
Adjusted EPS was $0.65, compared to $0.54 in the year-ago quarter.
Operating income was $7.0 billion.
Adjusted operating income was $7.5 billion.
Adjusted EBITDA was $12.3 billion, up 5.2% year over year.
Free cash flow (non-GAAP) was $4.7 billion, compared to $4.4 billion in the year-ago quarter.
Advanced Connectivity service revenue was $23.5 billion, up 5.1% year over year.
Advanced Connectivity EBITDA (non-GAAP) was $12.0 billion, up 8.0%.
The company added over 1 million Advanced Connectivity customers.
Total consumer and business Advanced Connectivity internet net adds were 646,000, comprised of 367,000 fiber and 279,000 fixed wireless.
Postpaid phone net adds were 432,000.
Legacy segment revenues declined 25.9% year over year to $1.6 billion.
The Legacy revenue decline was driven by lower demand as the company decommissions its copper-based network.
Latin America segment revenues increased 16.1% year over year to $1.2 billion.
The Latin America revenue increase was primarily driven by postpaid wireless subscriber growth and favorable foreign exchange rates.
For full-year 2026, the company expects adjusted EPS of $2.25 to $2.35.
For full-year 2026, the company expects adjusted EBITDA growth in the 3% to 4% range.
Long-term guidance for 2026-2028 includes annual capital investment (non-GAAP) in the $23 billion to $24 billion range.
Long-term guidance for 2026-2028 includes service revenue growth in the low-single-digit range annually.
Free cash flow (non-GAAP) is projected at $18 billion+ in 2026, $19 billion+ in 2027, and $21 billion+ in 2028.
Total debt was $144.0 billion at the end of the second quarter.
Net debt (non-GAAP) was $126.4 billion at the end of the second quarter.
The company returned $4.1 billion to shareholders in the second quarter.
The second-quarter shareholder returns included approximately $2.2 billion in common share repurchases.
AT&T plans to return $45 billion+ to shareholders during 2026-2028.
The 2026-2028 capital return plan includes approximately $10 billion in share repurchases during 2026.
Legacy EBITDA (non-GAAP) is expected to turn negative after 2027.
The company expects its net debt-to-adjusted EBITDA ratio (non-GAAP) to return to the 2.5x range within approximately three years following the closing of its transaction with EchoStar.
